questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this service authenticates drivers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A rider's access token, issued by the same auth server with the same key and audience but with typ='rider', is sent to /v1/trips/:tripId/accept. What happens?
choices: Accepted, because signature, issuer and audience all verify
Accepted only if a matching session key exists in Redis
Rejected with 401 invalid_token by the typ check, before Redis is consulted

questions.prompt: A driver logs out and then reuses the same, unexpired access token 10 seconds later. What happens?
choices: It works until the JWT's exp passes, since JWTs are stateless
401 session_revoked, because logout set the session key to 'revoked' and every request checks it
503, because the revoked key confuses the directory
It works for up to clockToleranceSec seconds

questions.prompt: What is the tradeoff of treating a missing Redis session key ('unknown') the same as 'revoked'?
choices: Valid tokens are rejected if session keys are evicted or expire before the JWT does, so availability is traded for strict revocation
Revoked drivers can keep accepting trips for 24 hours
Every request needs two Redis round trips
Expired JWTs are accepted while Redis is down
